textual.observation: The speaker instructs viewers to transfer EOS from Binance or another source into Plus Token, including copying and submitting a tag, in order to activate AIDoc.

evidence.quote: If you want to deposit EOS to activate your AIDoc, must copy the tag and must fill up the tag when you transfer your EOS from Binance or from anywhere into Plus Token okay

textual.context: Presented as an app walkthrough and operational guidance; whether this is promotion, neutral explanation, or another context is unclear from the supplied records.
textual.potential_relevance: A cryptocurrency transfer to a named platform is explicitly linked to an activation condition and a required transfer tag, creating a task-relevant payment/activation relationship for later assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish whether the transfer occurred, whether activation or any other outcome was obtained, who controls the destination, or whether the instruction is safe or fraudulent.

textual.observation: The speaker reports that the app's deposit and withdrawal labels are reversed and tells viewers to use the withdrawal button to obtain an EOS deposit address and tag.

evidence.quote: the withdrawal actually is the deposit and deposit actually is withdraw
if you want to deposit EOS, you click right now, it's the withdrawal button, so you will have the address for EOS and also the tag

textual.context: The speaker characterizes this as a translation or interface mistake and says it was reported to the company.
textual.potential_relevance: The stated mismatch between the displayed control and the intended deposit function is directly connected to a cryptocurrency-transfer instruction, warranting later assessment of the interface and destination correspondence.
textual.limitations: Only the speaker's account is available; the actual app interface, address, tag, transaction flow, and whether the labels were later corrected are not provided.

visual.observation: A cryptocurrency deposit screen visibly shows a QR code, a deposit address label, a required numeric tag, and a warning stating: "The label need to be filled when the money is transferred, otherwise the money would not be recorded in the account. Please don't transfer the EOS from EOS account, otherwise there are no ways to find the money back."
visual.context: Visible cryptocurrency-wallet deposit interface; whether this is a live transaction, demonstration, or tutorial is unclear.
visual.potential_relevance: The screen links a requested cryptocurrency transfer to entering a required tag and states that omitting the tag may prevent crediting the account, while also warning that a specified transfer route may be unrecoverable.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish that any transfer occurred, who controls the destination, whether the address or tag is legitimate, or whether any funds were lost. The QR code, address, and tag were not independently verified.

evidence.quote: Because next 7 days the company already do the announcement asking offers, testing ahm checking out everything inside the app any problem that we will report to the company and they will change it and they will fix it

evidence.quote: And I already reported to the company They will change it very soon

visual_context_notes.observation: The deposit screen includes an explicit warning about entering the label/tag and about transferring EOS from an EOS account, with no visible outcome shown.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it presents a PlusToken 2.0 launch and instructs viewers to transfer EOS, enter a tag, and activate AIDoc through that transfer. The displayed warning says an incorrectly handled transfer may not be credited or recoverable, while the speaker frames the reversed deposit and withdrawal wording as an app error reported for correction.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The video links cryptocurrency funding to activating AIDoc and describes cryptocurrency exchange operations. This is the closest supplied subtype because it presents a funded cryptocurrency workflow, although the evidence does not establish a bot, automated trading, profit, or a completed transfer.
